currentContext.expansion: Aditya Birla Capital (ABCL) is a listed, systemically important non-deposit taking NBFC that acts as the holding company for the group's financial-services businesses, offering loans, investments, insurance and payments through its subsidiaries and JVs across the customer lifecycle. Rather than physical plant/capex, its 'expansion' is distribution- and balance-sheet-led: a nationwide network of over 1,740 branches, more than 200,000 agents/channel partners and several bank partners, powered by over 68,000 employees. Management states it is well-positioned to accelerate growth across all lines of business on the back of a strong risk architecture, robust capital and liquidity management and high governance standards. To fund this growth, members are being asked (Notice of the 19th AGM) to raise the Company's borrowing powers and asset charge/security limits to a ceiling of Rs 2,00,000 Crore (Two Lakh Crore) and to approve issuance of Non-Convertible Debentures on a private placement basis. Management frames the outlook for financial services as structurally promising, driven by rising financial inclusion, digital adoption, retail SIP/mutual-fund participation, untapped rural life-insurance potential and post-Covid traction in health insurance, presenting a runway for innovation, expansion and long-term value creation.
currentContext.mdna: Management attributes a strong operating performance in FY26 to its diversified business model, citing momentum across all businesses|Health insurance is called out as a growth engine, with the company reaching a 13.7% market share among SAHI players

risks.risk: Asset-quality pressure in NBFC retail-unsecured and MFI books
risks.note: Management flags retail unsecured and microfinance as segments where NBFCs face asset-quality stress; deterioration here directly hits the ~Rs 2 Lakh Crore consolidated lending book.

risks.risk: Interest-rate and margin pressure in housing finance amid real-estate volatility
risks.note: HFCs are flagged as exposed to real-estate volatility, regulatory tightening and margin compression from falling interest rates.

Expanding scale of digital financial services, cloud-based infrastructure and interconnected systems has exponentially increased the possibility of cyberattacks; named a key vulnerability across the group.
Life insurers flagged for low policy persistency, investment volatility, evolving regulatory norms affecting product design/profitability, and rising customer complaints from mis-selling.

risks.risk: Health-insurance claims, fraud and pricing-regulation risk
risks.note: Health insurers contend with rising claims, medical inflation, fraud, regulatory constraints on pricing and post-pandemic underwriting complexity.

risks.risk: Regulatory, governance and compliance risk in a highly regulated NBFC
risks.note: BRSR identifies Corporate Governance & Business Ethics as a material risk; evolving prudential norms, product guidelines and ESG disclosures demand agile compliance, with gaps potentially causing fines, penalties and reputational damage.

risks.risk: Market and credit-cycle sensitivity of asset-management flows
risks.note: Mutual-fund business is vulnerable to market fluctuations, credit risk from stressed sectors and shifting investor preferences, affecting the ~Rs 4.36 Lakh Crore domestic QAAUM.

Management notes the prevailing credit environment and general macroeconomic factors playing out across sectors as the backdrop against which its integrated risk and governance framework must withstand economic and credit cycles.

hero.oneLiner: Aditya Birla Capital is a listed, systemically important non-deposit-taking NBFC that acts as the holding company for the Aditya Birla group's diversified financial-services franchise spanning lending, asset management, insurance and payments.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Aditya Birla Capital is a listed, systemically important non-deposit-taking NBFC that acts as the holding company for the Aditya Birla group's diversified financial-services franchise spanning lending, asset management, insurance and payments.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: ABCL provides a comprehensive suite of financial solutions across loans, investments, insurance and payments through its subsidiaries and JVs, serving customers across their lifecycles. Its standalone NBFC is among the top 5 diversified NBFCs in India, operating four lending verticals (personal & consumer, unsecured business, secured business, and corporate/mid-market), complemented by group asset management, life insurance, housing finance and health insurance businesses. The franchise has nationwide reach through 1,740+ branches, 200,000+ agents/channel partners and bank partners, powered by over 68,000 employees.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Aditya Birla Finance Limited (ABFL) — subsidiary: Erstwhile wholly owned subsidiary (NBFC lending); amalgamated with the Company under an NCLT-sanctioned Scheme of Amalgamation, effective 1st April 2025, with all its assets and liabilities transferred to and vested in ABCL
- Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC Limited — subsidiary: Asset management business; equity-accounted for Ind AS statutory reporting (not line-by-line consolidated); Company sold a partial stake
- Aditya Birla Insurance Brokers Limited — subsidiary: Insurance broking business; entire stake sold (gain treated as an exceptional/one-off item)

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Personal & Consumer:** Personal Loans, Consumer Loans, Check-out Financing, Co-branded Credit Card
- **Unsecured Business:** Business Loans, Supply Chain Finance, B2B Digital Platform, Business Overdraft, Udyog Plus (MSME digital trade-credit platform)
- **Secured Business:** Retail & SME LAP, LRD (Lease Rental Discounting), Small Ticket Secured & Micro LAP, Working Capital Loans, Loan Against Securities (LAS), Loan Against Property (LAP)
- **Corporate/Mid-Market:** Capex/WC Funding, Structured Finance, Developer Financing, Project Finance, Term Loans
- **Group financial services:** Asset management (mutual funds), Life insurance, Housing finance, Health insurance, Wealth solutions

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Retail and SME borrowers (secured MSME, salaried professionals, emerging income segment)
- Corporate groups across renewable energy, roads & transport, pharmaceuticals, FMCG, automotive, education and specialty chemicals
- Cat A / A+ real-estate developers (developer financing in select markets)
- Semi-urban and SME cluster geographies; corporate/mid-market concentrated in top 6-7 cities
- Nationwide India (financial inclusion, underserved and rural markets for insurance)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management attributes a strong operating performance in FY26 to its diversified business model, citing momentum across all businesses
- Health insurance is called out as a growth engine, with the company reaching a 13.7% market share among SAHI players

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Operate as a systemically important non-deposit taking NBFC and the holding company of the Aditya Birla group's financial services businesses, offering a comprehensive suite of solutions across loans, investments, insurance and payments to serve customers across their lifecycles
- Pursue a diversified financial-services model spanning NBFC lending, asset management, life insurance, housing finance and health insurance through its subsidiaries and JVs
- Leverage a nationwide distribution footprint of over 1,740 branches, more than 200,000 agents/channel partners and multiple bank partners to reach customers across India
- Prudent risk management and capital protection form the bedrock of the approach, with the aim of delivering risk-calibrated and sustainable returns across businesses in line with risk appetite. Under the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Policy (ICAAP), the Company assesses risks, risk mitigants and capital requirements for present and future periods, providing an aggregated view of capital position and ensuring adequate capital buffers are in place to address business exigencies. As a systemically important non-deposit-taking NBFC-ICC regulated by the RBI, capital and risk are managed within a defined risk appetite framework; no explicit dividend, buyback or payout policy is stated in the provided text.
- Actively promoting renewable-energy financing to drive adoption of clean-energy solutions and contribute to a low-carbon economy.
- Extending affordable credit to underserved segments (retail, SMEs/MSMEs, rural populations, women entrepreneurs, youth) to support business growth, livelihood creation and financial inclusion.
- Board of Directors and Risk Management Committee provide active oversight of ESG-related risks and opportunities, with established governance frameworks and policies.
- BRSR core indicators independently assured (Reasonable Assurance) by DNV Business Assurance India Pvt. Ltd.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Aditya Birla Capital (ABCL) is a listed, systemically important non-deposit taking NBFC that acts as the holding company for the group's financial-services businesses, offering loans, investments, insurance and payments through its subsidiaries and JVs across the customer lifecycle. Rather than physical plant/capex, its 'expansion' is distribution- and balance-sheet-led: a nationwide network of over 1,740 branches, more than 200,000 agents/channel partners and several bank partners, powered by over 68,000 employees. Management states it is well-positioned to accelerate growth across all lines of business on the back of a strong risk architecture, robust capital and liquidity management and high governance standards. To fund this growth, members are being asked (Notice of the 19th AGM) to raise the Company's borrowing powers and asset charge/security limits to a ceiling of Rs 2,00,000 Crore (Two Lakh Crore) and to approve issuance of Non-Convertible Debentures on a private placement basis. Management frames the outlook for financial services as structurally promising, driven by rising financial inclusion, digital adoption, retail SIP/mutual-fund participation, untapped rural life-insurance potential and post-Covid traction in health insurance, presenting a runway for innovation, expansion and long-term value creation.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Diversified financial-services conglomerate model spanning lending, asset management and insurance under one holding company, enabling cross-sell across the ABC customer ecosystem
- Among top 5 diversified NBFCs in India with scale and one of the fastest-growing AUM at this size
- Best-in-class asset quality and prudent risk management (declining Stage 2 & 3 loans, best-in-class credit costs) with an integrated risk & governance framework tested across credit cycles
- Strong distribution moat: 1,740+ branches, 200,000+ agents/channel partners, bank partnerships and rising direct/digital origination
- AI/ML embedded across sourcing, underwriting, servicing and collections (AI calling bots, fraud detection, credit copilots, straight-through processing) driving productivity and lower flow rates
- Proprietary Udyog Plus digital MSME platform with leading position on TReDS exchanges
- Highest-rated funding profile (long-term AAA, short-term A1+ by CRISIL/ICRA/India Ratings) supporting low cost of funds and well-matched ALM

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Asset-quality pressure in NBFC retail-unsecured and MFI books — Management flags retail unsecured and microfinance as segments where NBFCs face asset-quality stress; deterioration here directly hits the ~Rs 2 Lakh Crore consolidated lending book.
- Interest-rate and margin pressure in housing finance amid real-estate volatility — HFCs are flagged as exposed to real-estate volatility, regulatory tightening and margin compression from falling interest rates.
- Cyber-security and technology risk — Expanding scale of digital financial services, cloud-based infrastructure and interconnected systems has exponentially increased the possibility of cyberattacks; named a key vulnerability across the group.
- Life-insurance persistency and mis-selling risk — Life insurers flagged for low policy persistency, investment volatility, evolving regulatory norms affecting product design/profitability, and rising customer complaints from mis-selling.
- Health-insurance claims, fraud and pricing-regulation risk — Health insurers contend with rising claims, medical inflation, fraud, regulatory constraints on pricing and post-pandemic underwriting complexity.
- Regulatory, governance and compliance risk in a highly regulated NBFC — BRSR identifies Corporate Governance & Business Ethics as a material risk; evolving prudential norms, product guidelines and ESG disclosures demand agile compliance, with gaps potentially causing fines, penalties and reputational damage.
- Market and credit-cycle sensitivity of asset-management flows — Mutual-fund business is vulnerable to market fluctuations, credit risk from stressed sectors and shifting investor preferences, affecting the ~Rs 4.36 Lakh Crore domestic QAAUM.
- Macroeconomic and credit-environment exposure — Management notes the prevailing credit environment and general macroeconomic factors playing out across sectors as the backdrop against which its integrated risk and governance framework must withstand economic and credit cycles.
